decisions.summary: The exemption rule matches :is(path, circle) where the wash rule it overrides matches the wider filled-element set.
decisions.why: FR-001 exempts 'the lit bund-beans class's filled shapes'. The class draws circles only (settlement/fields/comb.py _comb_draw_beads), so path+circle covers every filled shape the class has today and nothing that exists keeps the wash. The seam - a future bund-beans shape of another element type silently keeping the wash - is the fail-safe direction spec D1 already chose.

decisions.summary: The new rule is placed after the wash rule so it wins by order, and sets fill-opacity: 1.
decisions.why: FR-001 asks for the vector page's fill opacity; the bead circles carry no fill-opacity attribute, so the vector page paints them at 1 and the constant matches. Cascade order is CSS mechanics the spec leaves to the implementation.

decisions.summary: The hit discs are excluded by :not([fill="none"]), the same test the wash uses; the group's 0.85 opacity is not named by the rule.
decisions.why: FR-001 requires the hit discs to stay unpainted and D2 requires the 0.85 group opacity to stay; the page writer emits hit shapes with fill="none", so the exclusion is exact and nothing narrows.

decisions.summary: page_lit.measure's --vector loop presses Control+= through page.keyboard.press in place of mouse.move + mouse.wheel; ZOOM_STEPS stays as the cap; the docstring says the key and why not the wheel.
decisions.why: FR-004 settles the key (Ctrl with the plus key) and the step cap; '=' is the unshifted plus key the page's own keydown handler reads.

decisions.summary: _FakePage gains a keyboard whose press logs; the two zoom-loop stub tests assert presses rather than wheel turns.
decisions.why: FR-005's last clause asks the stub test to mirror the key presses.

decisions.summary: CHANGED since round 1: the page-lit browser test measures the two-class halves page through a 300 by 300 viewport rather than 100 by 100, because at 100 the page's fixed zoom buttons covered most of the lit half; the share test lights the paddy, the half the buttons do not touch; raster asserted, and the vector case asserts mode == vector and zoom > 1.
decisions.why: FR-005 asks for 'a small viewport over the two-class synthetic map' whose opening view is raster mode, raster asserted, and the --vector case asserting vector reached with a zoom above the opening view - it fixes no viewport number and names no class for the share test. Research R1 records that 300 by 300 still opens below the raster switch on that 200-unit map (screen scale 1.5 against the picture's 2 per map unit) and that one doubling reaches vector, so every clause of FR-005 is still carried; nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: _driver._synthetic() gains one <circle r="1.4" fill="#2F6B35"/> tagged 'bund beans' on clear ground; the new test shrinks the viewport, presses fit, asserts data-mode raster, reads the wash on the lit paddy's rect and full on the lit bead circle, then restores the viewport and asserts both full on the vector page.
decisions.why: FR-005 asks for exactly this element and these assertions; the radius and color match the shipped bead, and restoring the viewport is a means of reaching the vector page that the spec leaves open.

decisions.summary: The interactive index's raster row and the tools index's page-lit row each gain one clause.
decisions.why: FR-006 asks for both rows to say the new thing; the length is not specified.

decisions.summary: RESOLVED since round 1: the plan's last Design bullet and tasks.md T04 now say SC-002 is decided by the R1 contact sheet RE-TAKEN on the shipped Inashiro page at its opening view with the shipped stylesheet, looked at by the session and recorded in tasks.md with the GM's eye final on the map itself; `make page-lit CLASS="bund beans"` is the subordinate check that no other class moved, stated as unable to decide the criterion because a washed bead already moves past its threshold; SC-003 is `make page-lit ... VECTOR=1` reporting mode: vector.
decisions.why: This is now the accepted spec's SC-002 and SC-003 in their own terms, including the spec's statement that the tool cannot decide SC-002, and it answers the GM's request on its own ground - the complaint is that the beads 'don't visible light up ... zoomed out', which only a look at the picture settles. tasks.md T04 carries the same wording, so nothing survives of the round-1 narrowing that named page-lit as the instrument for SC-002. The plan decides nothing here that the spec had not already settled.

decisions.summary: The Constitution Check takes the regression baseline to be the green `make done` the run log records from before this feature started, rather than a fresh detached-worktree run; the round-1 '8 hours' figure was removed in this pass.
decisions.why: Neither the request nor the accepted spec settles which baseline run is used, and SC-005's requirement of a green `make done` and a green `make page-check` is untouched, so this narrows nothing that was asked. The removal of the unsourced figure changes no decision; whether a run-log baseline satisfies Principle XIII is a gate question rather than a fidelity one.

decisions.summary: Constitution Check: the asset half is proved by `make page-check` and the tool half by `make done` (page_lit.py is engine code); the delta routes GATED (LOCAL-GATED), with page.css owing page-check at push; no pool manifest moves, so no settlement-review is owed.
decisions.why: SC-005 states all of this in the accepted spec - page-check green for the stylesheet, done green for the tool, no manifest moved so no settlement-review, lands GATED. The plan restates rather than decides.
